solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of speech, 'for richer, for poorer'

definitions.text: Part of speech, 'for richer, for poorer'

parts.words: Part of speech, 'for richer, for poorer'
parts.note: the wedding-vow phrase is part of a spoken vow, but grammatically richer and poorer are both forms of degree built on rich and poor

explanation.surface: A quotation from the marriage vows, presented as if lifted from a wedding speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' suggests nouns and verbs or a section of an address; the quoted words are each the -er grading form of an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar names the -er form of an adjective, as in richer or poorer, by this term for its degree.

clue.text: Sponsor, if I cease taking crack

indicators.note: the closing words take in, or hold, a run of letters spanning sponsor, if, I and cease

explanation.surface: A backer threatens to withdraw if someone stops using drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug the sponsor objects to, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a small opening or gap, and that is what this word for a hole or aperture names.

clue.text: Stranger sound following exercise clutching huge behind

indicators.note: the spoken piece comes after the exercise-and-huge piece
the exercise letters hold the huge abbreviation between them

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
OS is outsize, the clothing size for huge

indicators.note: the word for stranger is to be taken as it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: stranger means eerier, more weird

explanation.surface: An odd noise follows a workout in which someone grips something enormous from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger sound' means a word that sounds like 'eerier', not anything strange about a noise; 'huge' is the outsize clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind as a noun is the buttocks or rear, and the posterior is a polite word for that part of the body.

clue.text: Show regret embracing first woman endlessly

indicators.note: the regret word wraps itself around the cut-down woman's name

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: the last letter of the name is lopped off

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone shows remorse while hugging the first woman for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' reads as 'forever' in the surface, but it is a cut: the name loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances is a type of stage show.

clue.text: 'Plod' apprehends, catching one with Ecstasy

indicators.note: the drug letter is added alongside at the end
the word for apprehends catches the one numeral inside it

parts.note: to apprehend someone is to trap or catch them
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A policeman (Plod) arrests someone found carrying a single Ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: Plod is British slang for the police (after Mr Plod in Noddy), but here it is the verb to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk wearily or heavily, and to trudge about tiredly is the same idea.

clue.text: Protection from cover and awning

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from across the words cover, and and awning

explanation.surface: Seeking shelter under a cover and an awning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awning' looks like the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed porch along the side of a house gives shelter, or protection, from sun and rain.

clue.text: Wandering through Italy, sorry, not hot

parts.note: per means through or by way of
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: the hot letter is not to be included in the word for sorry

parts.note: sorry in the sense of pitiful, pathetic
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A traveller wanders through Italy, apologising that it is not warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorry' is an apology on the surface but means pitiful here.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant who travels from place to place is described with this adjective for roving about.

clue.text: Oval building not entirely about America

indicators.note: the word for about is not complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: circa means about, approximately
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A partly finished oval building with American connections.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena for chariot racing was a long oval building with tiered seats, the original of the term.

clue.text: Education that is provided first by special schools

indicators.note: the provided word is placed before the that-is abbreviation

parts.note: provided means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: A statement about education provided first by special schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb: teaches, improves.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them, and to improve someone morally or intellectually is a near synonym.

clue.text: This helps through giving renewed ardour initially!

definitions.text: This helps through giving renewed ardour initially!

parts.note: via means through, by way of

indicators.note: only the opening letters of giving, renewed and ardour are used

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of a pill that restores passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known impotence drug helps men by restoring sexual performance, the renewed ardour the clue describes.

clue.text: Right slam always inside ring

indicators.note: the always word goes inside the combination of right and slam

parts.note: to slam someone is to criticise or berate them
ever means always

explanation.surface: A boxer's right-hand blow lands repeatedly inside the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slam' and 'ring' suggest boxing; slam means criticise and ring is the verb to resound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or a voice that rings echoes and resounds, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Bank on the cards holding clubs

indicators.note: the phrase for on the cards holds the clubs letter within it

parts.note: on the cards means likely, in line for happening
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A card player relies on what is in their hand, including clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank on' reads as rely on, but 'Bank' alone is the definition, a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth is a slope, and a slope or gradient is also called by this word.

clue.text: Outside prison, siege ends after charge

indicators.note: the end letters of siege come after the prison word

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, outside
pen is a word for an enclosure or prison

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of siege are taken

explanation.surface: Outside a prison, a siege comes to an end after a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a military attack ending the siege; it is the definition, a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a price or cost paid, and the outlay of money spent is another word for that.

clue.text: 'I will', shortly to be heard here?

indicators.note: the shortened form is to be taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: the contracted form of I will is I'll

explanation.surface: A bride or groom's 'I will' spoken briefly at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The vow is said at the altar, reached up the central walkway of the church, so 'here?' points there.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's central walkway is where the couple stand to say their vows, the place pointed to.

clue.text: Curse Devil, then Church is back in charge

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: the turned church letters go inside the charge word

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is turned around so it reads backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Cursing the Devil while a church is back in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To call down evil on someone is to curse them, which this formal verb expresses.

clue.text: Trembling? Drink up and gasp swallowing vermouth

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the drink word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat

indicators.note: the gasp word swallows the vermouth abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone shaking, finishing a drink and gasping after downing vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink up' looks like an instruction to finish a glass; up reverses LAP in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something throbbing or quivering, like a racing heart, is described with this word for palpitating.

clue.text: Fugitive's record with time in border line

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the time word sits inside the border-and-line combination

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A runaway's criminal record and a sentence served in a border line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fugitive' looks like a runaway, but as an adjective it means fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective fugitive means fleeting or transient, lasting only a short while.

clue.text: Little hard with coal perhaps lacking energy

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
and means with, together with

indicators.note: the energy letter is missing from the fuel word

parts.note: coal is an example of fuel
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A small amount of hard coal, short of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity, a few, can be called a little, and this word for what one hand holds means that.

clue.text: Show bottom around mid-evening thus producing wind

indicators.note: the show-bottom word goes around the middle letter and the thus word

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare bottom

indicators.note: only the middle letter of evening is used

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: Someone bares their backside midway through the evening and breaks wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' suggests flatulence after the mooning; it is the seasonal wind of South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South and Southeast Asia that brings heavy rains is called by this name.

clue.text: Conservative member's ascent

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's rise to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests an MP; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a rise or upward journey, as of a mountain.

clue.text: Tongue lash, in the manner of Navy

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a lash
a la, French, means in the manner of

explanation.surface: A tongue-lashing delivered in naval style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue lash' reads as a scolding; Tongue alone is the definition, a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and this is the language of Catalonia in north-east Spain.

clue.text: Burning lessens, containing fires

indicators.note: the two words contain the letters across their join

explanation.surface: As burning lessens, fires are contained.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire on a hearth, so the plural names household fires.

clue.text: Period when bats fly about?

parts.note: the bats are cricket bats, swung freely during a team's turn at the crease, not flying mammals

explanation.surface: A question about the time of night when bats are on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's term for a side's turn to bat, during which batsmen swing their bats.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a team's or player's spell of batting is the period when bats are swung about.

clue.text: Small border plant

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A small plant growing in a garden border.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass-like plant of wet ground is an example of a plant.

clue.text: One, for example, in between

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes in the between word

parts.note: inter- means between

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in between, one for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a pronoun; it is the number, an example of a whole number.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one is an example of a whole number, so it is defined by example.

clue.text: Provide a couple of fines joining ring road

indicators.note: the ring and road pieces join on after the fines

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencils, so two fines give two Fs
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A motorist must pay a couple of fines for joining the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide' fits 'afford' in the sense afford an opportunity, give.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford someone a view or a chance is to give or supply it to them.

clue.text: Unnatural impregnation left males time for complaint

parts.note: AI is artificial insemination
men are males

explanation.surface: A grievance after artificial insemination left the men short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests a grievance; it is the medical sense, an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: Secret family fortune's endless with eye-opener

indicators.note: the eye's first letter is added on

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: the last letter of the fortune word is dropped

parts.note: fortune means destiny, fate

indicators.note: only the first letter of eye is used

explanation.surface: A family's fortune is unending, which is quite an eye-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' reads as a surprise, but splits into eye plus its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in secret is covert or hidden, which is what this word means.
